title: Business Builder / Venture Research & Launch Assistant
description:
I’m looking for a resourceful, entrepreneurial Business Builder / Venture Research & Launch Assistant to help me identify, validate, and begin building a profitable business.



My ultimate goal is to create an additional source of income that can grow over time and eventually give me more control over my schedule and free up my time.



I am not looking for someone to sell me a generic business idea, dropshipping course, get-rich-quick strategy, or AI-generated list of “10 businesses you can start.”



I want someone who can actually research opportunities, evaluate them realistically, help me select the strongest business model, and then assist with building and launching it.



The Goal



The initial goal is to identify a business opportunity that:



* Has realistic revenue potential

* Has relatively low startup costs

* Can be started while I am still working full-time

* Can eventually be systemized, delegated, or partially automated

* Does not require me to personally perform every task forever

* Has room to scale

* Solves an actual problem people or businesses will pay to solve

* Can realistically generate its first revenue without requiring years of development



I am open to service businesses, digital businesses, B2B opportunities, online businesses, and other legitimate models.



I am especially interested in opportunities where my existing professional experience, skills, or knowledge could create an advantage, but I am also open to opportunities outside of my current industry if the business case is strong.



Phase 1: Business Research & Validation



Your first responsibility will be helping me identify and evaluate potential business opportunities.



For each serious opportunity, I want research covering:



* What the business actually sells

* Who the target customer is

* What problem the business solves

* Why customers would pay for it

* How much competitors charge

* Who the major competitors are

* Startup costs

* Estimated operating costs

* Potential profit margins

* Difficulty of acquiring customers

* How customers could be acquired

* How quickly the business could reasonably generate revenue

* What parts of the business could eventually be automated or delegated

* Major risks or barriers to entry

* What would make our version of the business different or better



I want recommendations based on actual research and business logic, not trends or hype.



Phase 2: Business Model Development



Once we identify the strongest opportunity, you will help me turn the idea into an actual business model.



This may include:



* Defining the target customer

* Developing the service or product offering

* Creating pricing packages

* Developing the value proposition

* Researching competitors

* Identifying potential customer acquisition channels

* Creating basic financial projections

* Mapping startup expenses

* Creating a simple launch strategy

* Developing processes and workflows

* Identifying tools or software needed to operate the business



The business should be designed with simplicity and scalability in mind.



Phase 3: Build & Launch



After the business model is approved, I want assistance actually building it.



Depending on the business, responsibilities may include:



* Business and competitor research

* Setting up operational systems

* Creating lead lists

* Researching potential customers

* Developing prospect databases

* Setting up a CRM or tracking system

* Creating standard operating procedures

* Building simple workflows and automations

* Coordinating freelancers or vendors

* Helping set up business tools and software

* Researching website or landing-page solutions

* Assisting with launch preparation

* Tracking leads, outreach, customers, and revenue

* Identifying areas that can be outsourced or automated



I want someone who is comfortable going beyond research and helping turn ideas into execution.



A Major Priority: Building Something That Does Not Depend Entirely on Me



One of my primary objectives is creating a business that can eventually operate without requiring my constant involvement.



As we build the business, I want you to continually identify:



* Tasks that can be automated

* Tasks that can eventually be delegated to virtual assistants or contractors

* Processes that need SOPs

* Systems that reduce manual work

* Ways to make customer acquisition repeatable

* Ways to create recurring or repeat revenue

* Opportunities to increase revenue without proportionally increasing my workload



I understand that building a business requires work upfront. I am not expecting passive income overnight.



However, I specifically want to avoid creating another job for myself.



What I Am NOT Looking For



Please do not apply if your strategy consists primarily of recommending:



* Random dropshipping stores

* Crypto or trading

* Amazon automation schemes

* Expensive business courses

* MLMs

* Generic print-on-demand businesses

* “Passive income” schemes

* Businesses copied from TikTok or YouTube without research

* AI-generated business plans with no real market validation



I am looking for real business fundamentals, research, execution, and measurable progress.



Ideal Candidate



You may be a strong fit if you have experience in one or more of the following:



* Entrepreneurship

* Business development

* Startup operations

* Market research

* Lead generation

* Business strategy

* Virtual assistance

* Project management

* Digital marketing

* Sales operations

* Building online businesses

* Creating SOPs and operational systems

* Automation or no-code tools



You should be:



* Extremely resourceful

* Comfortable researching unfamiliar industries

* Analytical

* Organized

* Able to challenge weak ideas

* Comfortable working independently

* Focused on execution rather than endless planning

* Able to explain why an opportunity does or does not make business sense



I do not need someone who agrees with every idea I have.



If an idea is unlikely to work, I want you to tell me why and recommend something better.



Initial Project



This will begin as a 30-day business-building project.



During the first 30 days, I would like us to:



Week 1: Research and evaluate potential business opportunities.



Week 2: Select and validate the strongest business model.



Week 3: Build the offer, pricing, systems, customer-acquisition strategy, and launch infrastructure.



Week 4: Begin launching, prospecting, testing, and attempting to generate our first customers or revenue.



The exact timeline may change depending on the business we select, but I want this project to remain execution-focused.



When Applying



Please answer the following:



1. Tell me about something you have helped build from the ground up.

2. Have you helped launch or operate a small business before?

3. What types of businesses have you worked with?

4. If you were given a limited startup budget and needed to create a business capable of generating revenue relatively quickly, how would you approach the research?

5. How would you determine whether a business idea has real demand?

6. What would you research before recommending that I invest money into a business idea?

7. What tools do you use for market research, lead generation, automation, project management, or business operations?

8. How would you design a business so that the owner could eventually delegate much of the day-to-day work?

9. Give me one example of a business model you believe could be attractive today and briefly explain why. I am evaluating your thinking process, not simply the idea itself.



Please include the word “Builder” somewhere in your application so I know you read the entire posting.



I am looking for someone who thinks like an operator.



I don’t just want ideas.



I want someone who can help me research, validate, build, launch, measure, improve, and eventually systemize a real business.

description:

Role Summary

captions within our proprietary Approval system. You will ensure all brand assets meet

our high quality standards and align perfectly with client feedback. This is a fast-paced, remote role requiring a sharp eye for detail and quick turnaround times.





Key Responsibilities

Edit Content: Content needs to be edited within 24 hours after it has been generated or feedback has been left. You’ll be sent Approvals for each customer workspace that needs to have content edits. All edits will be completed with AI. You do not need graphic design experience. There are typically two rounds of edits:

First Round

Images: Make edits to any incorrect AI images (ex: extra hands, gibberish text, etc)

Captions: Make edits to captions that have errors.

Second Round

All edits to Images and Captions will be made based on the client’s feedback left on the Approvals

Additional Rounds (If needed)

All additional edits to Images and Captions will be made based on the client’s feedback left on the Approvals





Follow Up with Cloud Campaign Point of Contact

Once the First Round of content has been edited, alert the POC so they can share the edited content with the client.

Repeat for the Second Round and Additional Rounds, if needed.



Tools and Estimate Time:

Tools:

Approval - this will be
ed to the designated
 address once it has been generated

Approval Editor - 
/

You will enter the approval link into the editor, and then will be able to submit edits.





Estimated Time: Per client depends on how many workspaces CloudStudio is active. Below is a breakdown of how long it typically takes per workspace Approval.

First Round of Edits = 10-30 minutes per Approval

Second Round of Edits = 20-60 minutes per Approval

This heavily depends on how much feedback the client has left for editing.

Third Round of Edits = 10-30 minutes per Approval

This also depends on how much feedback the client has left for editing, but typically is lighter after the second round.



Tips for Editing Content:





When reviewing and editing the first round of AI generated content, we’re looking for the following things to revise:

If the caption does not follow the post strategy based on the Campaign Brief

If there are images with clear anatomical or physics issues

If there are images that obviously seem wrong for the brand

Example: While reviewing a restaurant’s content, there was one picture where it clearly looked like a table in someone's home instead of a restaurant table, and the food was an item the restaurant didn’t sell.





Approval Editor: Use words like “CRITICAL” and “STRICT” when editing images.

Example: CRITICAL: Ensure the packaging matches exactly what is displayed in reference images 2 - 3 and the dimensions correctly match the reference photos. Reference photo 2 shows the container that salads and grain bowls must be in. Reference photo 3 shows the container that soups must be in. Do NOT change the contents of the bowls from the original image. STRICT: All utensils must be plastic to-go utensils.

Experience should include:

2. Grading plans

4. Utility plans

title: Executive Assistant / Project Coordinator (Remote)
description:
About the role

The founder of a portfolio of ecommerce brands, and he's looking for a sharp, proactive Executive Assistant who also acts as a project coordinator across his business and personal life. This is not a task-execution VA role — it's a right-hand seat.



You'll own his calendar, drive his product-development and digital projects forward, keep his systems current, and handle the executive and personal admin that frees him to focus on high-level decisions.



The best person for this role anticipates what's needed before being asked, holds multiple projects in motion without dropping details, and communicates clearly in writing. If you take ownership and make things happen, you'll thrive here — and grow with the business.



What you'll own:

- Executive support

    * Manage his calendar — schedule, protect focus time, resolve conflicts

    * Prepare meeting agendas and briefing notes; chase follow-ups after his meetings

    * Support his inbox — draft replies, surface what needs him, keep it organized

    * Produce a daily morning brief: his calendar, decisions he needs to make, project status, and what he's waiting on

- Project coordination

    * Keep his product-development projects on track — maintain the timeline, flag slipping deadlines, and keep him updated on status (project tracking, not vendor management)

    * Coordinate digital projects (e.g., our DTC website build) — organize tasks, assets, and blockers

    * Manage creative and design deliverables (e.g., product photography) — brief, track, and chase to completion

    * Track our IP filing and compliance checklist so nothing advances out of sequence



- Systems & hiring admin

    * Keep our Notion workspace current — goals, tasks, and project trackers

    * Run hiring logistics — schedule interviews, collect scorecards, track candidates

    * Prepare research briefs and decision memos when I need to make a call



- Personal / life management

    * Book travel — flights, hotels, ground transport, full itineraries (business + personal)

    * Manage personal appointments, reservations, renewals, subscriptions, and reminders

    * Handle personal research and errands remotely — purchases, bookings, returns, vendor coordination



What this role does NOT include:

To keep scope clean, these are owned by other team members:

- Amazon Seller Central / marketplace operations

- Vendor and supplier relationships — including new sourcing partners — plus purchase orders, payments, freight, and logistics

- Finance, bookkeeping, and invoicing

- Social and affiliate marketing execution



Your product-development work is coordination and tracking only — keeping projects, timelines, and my decisions moving. Vendor and supplier relationships are owned separately.



Who you are:

- A proactive owner — you move work forward without being told each step, and flag problems before they grow

- Organized under pressure — you hold several projects in motion at once and don't drop details

- A clear writer — your written English is crisp and professional; you can draft a clean
, agenda, or brief on your own

- Trustworthy and discreet — you'll handle personal and sensitive information with judgment, and you know what to escalate

- Systems-minded — you're comfortable in project tools and pick up new software (including AI tools) quickly



Experience & skills

Required:

- 2+ years as an Executive Assistant to a founder or senior executive (entrepreneurial environment preferred)

- Demonstrated project or vendor coordination — you've run something end-to-end, not just completed assigned tasks

- Experience managing executive travel and personal/life admin

- Hands-on with a project/workspace tool — Notion strongly preferred (Asana, ClickUp, Monday, or Trello also considered)

- Excellent written and spoken English

- Reliable computer, fast and stable internet, quiet workspace



Nice to have:

- Exposure to ecommerce or DTC brands (helpful context, not required)

- Experience working with US-based founders or on US business hours

- Comfort with AI and automation tools



Tools you'll use:

Notion · Google Workspace (Calendar, Gmail, Drive) · Slack · project management tools · AI tools



How to apply:

(Read carefully — I'm looking for attention to detail and initiative.)



- Start your application with the word "Amanak" so I know you read this posting in full.

- In 3–4 sentences, tell me about a specific time you moved a project or solved a problem before being asked.

- Briefly describe your experience with Notion or a similar project tool.

- Include your expected monthly rate and your available working hours (with timezone).



Applications that don't follow these steps won't be reviewed.

title: Video Editor
description:
Social Media Video Editor + Content Strategist — Personal Brand



I’m looking for a high-level video editor with a strong understanding of social media to help take my personal brand to the next level.



I don’t just need someone who knows how to use editing software. I need someone who understands attention, hooks, storytelling, pacing, retention, and what makes people stop scrolling.



You should have a great eye for style, a fast turnaround time, and be comfortable producing multiple pieces of content per day.



What you'll be doing



You'll be working with a library of raw footage and turning it into polished, engaging social content, including:



* Instagram Reels / short-form videos

* Talking-head content

* B-roll with text overlays

* Carousels and static posts

* Educational content

* Story-driven videos

* Clips pulled from longer-form footage



Some projects will be straightforward. For example, I may give you several teleprompter takes and need you to comb through the footage, identify the strongest takes, remove mistakes, and turn them into a polished video.



Other projects will require much more creativity. I may give you raw footage with no exact script, and I need you to be able to watch it, identify the interesting story or idea, develop the hook, and turn it into something people actually want to watch.



I'm looking for someone who understands CONTENT — not just editing.



You should understand:



* How important the first 1–3 seconds are

* Hooks and curiosity

* Storytelling and pacing

* Retention and watch time

* Text placement and on-screen captions

* B-roll and pattern interrupts

* When an edit should be fast and punchy vs. simple and clean

* How to repurpose one piece of footage into multiple pieces of content

* Current short-form content styles and trends

* How to make content feel native to Instagram/TikTok rather than overly produced



Most importantly, I want someone who is willing to pay attention to the numbers. If something gets 2,000 views and something else gets 50,000, I want you asking:  Why? What was different about the hook? The topic? The edit? The pacing? The format? I want someone who learns from what performs, recognizes what flops, and continuously helps us make better content.



The goal



Ultimately, your job is to help me turn:



Raw footage ? great content ? consistent posting ? more views ? a stronger personal brand.



I want to be able to send you footage and trust that you're going to find the gold in it.



To apply



Please send me:



1. 3–5 examples of short-form content you've personally edited.

2. Links to any social media accounts you've helped grow or regularly created content for.

3. A short video introducing yourself and telling me about your experience.

4. Tell me about one Reel/TikTok you've edited that performed extremely well and WHY you think it worked.

5. Tell me what you would do if we posted 10 videos and 8 of them underperformed.



I'm looking for someone who is creative, fast, reliable, accountable, and obsessed with making better content.



If you're simply looking for someone to hand you exact timestamps and editing instructions for every video, this probably isn't the right position.



If you love taking a pile of raw footage and figuring out how to turn it into content people actually want to consume, I want to hear from you.
